utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We have this morning a conference in respect of the two accused, Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac. Appearances, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Alex Whiting for the Prosecution, along with Ms. Laurie Sartorio on my left, and our case manager, Lakshmie Walpita, on my right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Mr. Cermak, Mr. Prodanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I am appearing for General Cermak. My name is Cedo Prodanovic, and with me is my co-counsel, Ms. Jadranka Slokovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes. Mr. Separovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Good morning, Your Honour. I am attorney-at-law, Miroslav Separovic. With me is Mr. Goran Mikulicic, attorney-at-law, and we appear for General Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The accused are on pre-trial release, provisional release, there is no need for their appearance this morning. Now, this I believe is the fifth of the Status Conferences. It's called because of the requirement to have regular Status Conferences of this type. There was yesterday a Rule 65 ter meeting, and I've received a brief report on that from the Senior Legal Officer who conducted the conference. Could I indicate to the parties that I believe very shortly all Judges who are dealing with the matter will have completed their consideration of the motion that is outstanding on the amendment of the indictment and that it is my expectation that the decision in that issue is imminent. Now, we come to matters of disclosure. Perhaps Mr. Whiting, you might indicate the current state of the Prosecutor's position about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Of course, disclosure under 66(i)(i) has long been completed. With respect to 66(A)(ii), the Prosecution has disclosed all statements which fall under that Rule to the Defence, both in English and in B/C/S. So that that -- as of this time, disclosure is complete under that rule. And of course, as the Rule provides, to the extent that the Prosecution identifies additional witnesses that it intends to call at trial, it will disclose those statements in both languages promptly, immediately. I should say on this point that as Your Honour is no doubt aware, yesterday there was a question from Defence counsel about certain instances where the Prosecution disclosed videotapes of interviews of witnesses without a transcript, and there was a question from Defence counsel about that, whether a transcript was going to be prepared. The Prosecution has looked into that matter and has also spoken with Defence counsel. I believe we've resolved the matter. But for the satisfaction of the Court, what we have determined is that there are approximately eight or so interviews that were taken in 2005. The tape of the interview which contains of course both English and B/C/S has been disclosed and can be reviewed by Defence counsel. Transcripts have been requested for those tapes; however, they're not yet completed. And as soon as they are complete, they will be provided to Defence counsel. And I believe that that is - and Defence counsel can correct me if I'm wrong - but I believe that's satisfactory to Defence counsel. Moving through the other disclosure obligations. With respect to Rule 70, the Rule 70 disclosure has been completed with one exception. And the exception has to do with a group of documents that -- for which the Prosecution requested Rule 70 clearance from the United Nations headquarters last spring, but learned that in fact the United Nations headquarters did not have the authority to give the clearance. Even though the documents had been sent to the headquarters, it -- the clearance has to come from the country of the person who wrote the documents. And in this case it's the United Kingdom. A request has been made to the foreign office in London. I have followed-up on that request and I anticipate that that matter will be resolved within the next month. Rule 68 disclosure is ongoing. As I told the Senior Legal Officer yesterday, we have reviewed all of the materials directly related to this investigation to determine what, if any, material might fall under Rule 68. And all that material has been disclosed. And as the -- as the investigate -- as there is additional investigation or other documents are reviewed from other cases and Rule 68 material or potential Rule 68 material is identified, that material will of course be disclosed. And Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. then -- and the next step will be that we will undertake in consultation with the Defence to do some searches of the collection of witness statements and Rule 70 documents which are held by the Tribunal according to certain search terms. And it's the search terms that we will consult with the Defence about. And I think unless -- I think that covers all of the disclosure issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. Mr. Prodanovic, is there any matter concerning disclosure you would like to mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is nothing I wish to add to what my learned friend has just said. Yesterday at our 65 ter meeting we clarified everything and agreed on further steps to be taken. So there are no issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Separovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I can say the same as my colleague. Yesterday we agreed on everything, and I believe that all the technical difficulties have been solved and that what my learned friend has said will take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you indeed. Well, Mr. Whiting, that's a happy state of affairs for once. Now, the other thing I notice is the agreed facts. That seems not yet to be in such a happy condition. How do you see the position, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I -- there's been a little -- just a little bit of progress but I think there's hope for more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's certainly room for more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: There's certainly room for more. The Prosecution -- just for the record, the Prosecution sent a list of proposed agreed facts to the Defence on August 1st, and the Defence has responded on September 15th. And because there's two accused and one Prosecution, there is in fact very little overlap. I think it amounts to perhaps only three agreed facts out of 154 that all three parties agree to. However, individually each of the Defence counsel have agreed to more facts, and more importantly have proposed modifications to some of the facts which the Prosecution still has to consider. We have not had time yet to evaluate their proposals and look at them. But there's certainly room for progress there. And further, I think that certainly for the Defence counsel and to some extent for the Prosecution, the imminent decision about the amendment to the indictment may create further possibilities for agreed facts. I think Defence counsel have been reluctant to take final positions without knowing what the final indictment would be. So we're hopeful that further discussions will lead to further agreed -- additional agreed facts. And at the moment the ball is more or less in our court to evaluate the responses of the Defence and respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that's all in respect of facts which you have proposed. Has there been any proposal for the Prosecution to agreed facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, not -- only to the extent that the Defence has proposed modifications to ours. So those might be considered proposals from the Defence, but otherwise, no, not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prodanovic, I think Mr. Whiting has indicated that both you and Mr. Separovic would like to see the decision on the indictment before you reach any final decisions about agreed facts. I can understand that so that hopefully very shortly you'll be in a position to enter into more extensive consideration of agreement, both discussing it with Mr. Separovic and then negotiating perhaps with Mr. Whiting. Is there anything you'd want to add to the situation beyond that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Of course, the Defence is awaiting the definite version of the indictment, however this will not prevent us from anticipating this and reaching agreement on indisputable facts. We have sent our position not containing extensive material but there are some facts that are beyond dispute. And in view of the fact that there are some terminological differences, I don't know whether the problem is in translation or whether the OTP has a different view of certain terms. If we can agree on the terminology we can also agree on certain facts. So it was a kind of conditional agreement which, as we agreed with the OTP, we will clarify at a later stage. And, of course, matters will take their course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, hopefully the speed at which the matter takes its course can become faster shortly. Mr. Separovic, is there anything that you would like to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, our position is identical to the position of General Cermak's Defence on this matter, so I will not repeat what my colleague has said. When the objections are settled, then we can approach the agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Is there any further matter, Mr. Whiting, you would wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not from the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prodanovic, any further matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Separovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much, ladies and gentlemen, for your attendance and your assistance. I think when we next meet for a conference of this nature, it ought to be possible to contemplate that there is a fairly settled state of readied preparation for trial. We will plan toward that and hope that that is achieved. Thank you for your assistance, and I will now rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: adjourned at 9:17 a.m.
